description: Real-weather ETEX-1 mini run from ERA5 native model levels. Candidate uses the prepared 65x41x16 regular lat/lon meteorology with 16 fixed AGL levels and omega-derived w; pristine FLEXPART 11.1 uses 137 native hybrid levels with etadot.

candidate_transformation.description: ERA5 native 137 hybrid levels -> 16 fixed AGL levels (10-20000m); omega-derived w (Pa/s -> m/s); 0.25 deg regular lat/lon preparation; temporal interpolation by etex-run across the six prepared snapshots with a 900s candidate timestep

oracle_transformation.description: ERA5 native 137 hybrid levels retained for pristine FLEXPART 11.1; native etadot vertical velocity on the 0.25 deg regular lat/lon grid; fixed-sync Oracle integration with LSYNCTIME=900s

meteorology.note: Source ERA5 native model levels downloaded 2024-09-10; fixtures/etex/native-mini/ contains 6 snapshots (1994-10-23 15:00, 18:00, 21:00; 1994-10-24 00:00, 03:00, 06:00). DIGESTS.json in fixtures/etex/native-mini/ records SHA-256 of each GRIB file.

representation_differences.vertical_coordinate: Candidate meteorology: 16 fixed AGL levels [10,50,100,200,400,600,900,1300,1800,2500,3500,5000,7000,10000,14000,20000] m; Oracle meteorology: 137 native ERA5 hybrid model levels.
representation_differences.horizontal_grid: Candidate meteorology and Oracle GRIB use the same 0.25 deg regular lat/lon source grid (65x41 points, -8..8 deg lon and 43..53 deg lat). Concentration comparison uses the separate 64x40 OUTGRID declared in output_grid.
representation_differences.temporal_resolution: Candidate uses a fixed 900s integration timestep. Oracle uses fixed_sync_w (CTL=-5) with LSYNCTIME=900s; the raw COMMAND contains IFINE=4 but FLEXPART forces effective IFINE=1 for the w formulation.
representation_differences.wind_components: Candidate uses omega-derived w (pressure velocity converted to m/s); Oracle uses native etadot (eta-coordinate velocity).
representation_differences.pbl_diagnostics: Candidate uses surface/PBL fields prepared from ERA5 and the GPU PBL path; Oracle uses FLEXPART's native PBL diagnostics. The input-equivalence audit treats this as an unresolved scientific representation difference.
notes: Release, meteorology domain, simulation timestep and concentration output grid mirror the existing scripts/run-etex.sh mini pipeline.
These are structural representation differences, not an input-equivalence verdict.
ETEX uses the pinned inert SPECIES_024 contract; dry/wet removal is disabled on candidate and oracle paths.

known_input_equivalence_limitations.description: Existing ETEX evidence has not demonstrated candidate/oracle input equivalence; #52 must emit the authoritative gate verdict before parity scoring.

notes: Real ETEX-1 release and run geometry are mirrored from fixtures/etex/mini/config/RELEASES and scripts/etex/prepare_native_era5.py.

Horizontal release containment is inside the prepared 65x41 meteorology domain; strict 3D containment remains waived because the release spans 5-15m AGL while the candidate meteorology starts at the first sampled AGL level of 10m.
Real-weather surface fields are supplied by the ERA5 preparation pipeline; no static representative surface block is substituted.
Normal scripts/run-etex.sh mini uses the pristine unmodified FLEXPART 11.1 oracle; the #50 seedable validation oracle is a separate WIND-UNI-002 evidence lane.
No scientific parity claimed: INPUT_EQUIVALENCE_NOT_DEMONSTRATED remains authoritative until #52.

Oracle COMMAND preserves historical fixed-timestep semantics: CTL=-5 selects method=0/mintime=LSYNCTIME, LSYNCTIME=900s; FLEXPART selects the w formulation and forces effective IFINE=1 internally although the raw COMMAND contains IFINE=4.
